# Mantel

> Mantel is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later), controller-first game launcher for Windows handhelds. It is a console-style home screen that puts every installed game (Steam, Xbox / Game Pass / Microsoft Store, Epic Games, GOG, Ubisoft Connect and any other .exe) on one fullscreen shelf you drive with a gamepad. Games still launch through their own stores, so nothing gets reinstalled or reconfigured.

Mantel is built on and for the ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X and is meant for any Windows handheld or TV PC. It ships as a 64-bit Windows installer (`Mantel_x.y.z_x64-setup.exe`) on GitHub Releases. The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run (More info → Run anyway).

Key facts:

- Finds installed games on first launch, with no plugins and no per-store setup.
- Every screen works with a gamepad, the touchscreen or a keyboard. A control center closes games, restarts or powers off the device.
- Times every play session; with Steam or Xbox accounts connected it also brings in playtime from all devices and shows owned games that aren't installed.
- Minimizes while a game runs and comes back when it exits.
- Artwork comes from Steam and GOG, plus SteamGridDB with the user's own free key.
- Privacy: no servers and no telemetry. Steam and Xbox sign-in happen on Steam's and Microsoft's own pages. All data stays on the PC in `%APPDATA%\com.playmantel.launcher\`.
- Built with Tauri 2 (Rust) and React + TypeScript.
- Compared with Playnite: Mantel is narrower, a single fullscreen controller-first home screen with no plugins. Compared with the Xbox full screen experience: Mantel is an independent app that treats every store the same.
- Not affiliated with Valve, Microsoft, ASUS, Epic Games, GOG or Ubisoft.
